---
title: "Sample quality control"
subtitle: "RNA-seq, before differential expression"

params:
  qc: "sample_qc.Rds"     # output of sample_qc.R
  # metadata column for the group axis and colours; "" = the first
  group: ""
  # every sample is labelled in the PCA up to this many samples; flagged
  # samples are always labelled
  max_labels: 30
---

```{r load-libraries}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(ggplot2)
  library(patchwork)
  library(ggrepel)
  library(scales)
  library(reactable)
})
```

```{r import-datasets}
# Local preview:
# quarto preview sample_qc.qmd -P qc:<outdir>/sample_qc/sample_qc.Rds
qc <- readRDS(params$qc)

cfg <- qc$settings
samples <- qc$samples
samples$flagged <- samples$flags != ""

n_samples <- nrow(samples)
n_flagged <- sum(samples$flagged)

cat_cols <- qc$columns$column[qc$columns$type == "categorical"]
num_cols <- qc$columns$column[qc$columns$type == "continuous"]
```

```{r color-schema}
# Same colours as the transcriptome report: grey for reference levels
# (control, 0), then the palette in fixed order, never recycled
series_colours <- c(
  "#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#1baf7a", "#eda100",
  "#e87ba4", "#008300", "#6250d6", "#e34948"
)
ref_colour <- "#898781"
na_colour <- "#c9c8c2"
flag_colour <- "#fdf1e7"

# one-hue sequential ramp: light = low, dark = high
seq_low <- "#e6eefb"
seq_high <- "#0d366b"

# circle, triangle, square, diamond, down-triangle
point_shapes <- c(21, 24, 22, 23, 25)

is_ref <- function(lvls) tolower(lvls) %in% c("0", "control")
is_series <- function(lvls) !is_ref(lvls) & lvls != "NA"

level_colours <- function(x) {
  lvls <- levels(x)
  cols <- rep(ref_colour, length(lvls))
  cols[lvls == "NA"] <- na_colour
  cols[is_series(lvls)] <- series_colours[seq_len(sum(is_series(lvls)))]
  setNames(cols, lvls)
}

# More than three non-reference levels also get one point shape each
level_shapes <- function(x) {
  lvls <- levels(x)
  use <- sum(is_series(lvls)) > 3 && length(lvls) <= length(point_shapes)
  shapes <- if (use) point_shapes[seq_along(lvls)] else rep(21, length(lvls))
  setNames(shapes, lvls)
}

# Categorical columns with a colour for every level
colourable <- cat_cols[vapply(cat_cols, function(col) {
  sum(is_series(levels(samples[[col]]))) <= length(series_colours)
}, logical(1))]
plot_cols <- c(colourable, num_cols)
```

```{r group-column}
# The group on the x-axis of the metric plots and the colour of the lines,
# with missing values as their own level
samples$.all <- factor("All samples")

group_col <- if (params$group != "") {
  params$group
} else if (length(colourable) > 0) {
  colourable[1]
} else {
  ".all"
}

if (!group_col %in% c(colourable, ".all")) {
  stop(
    "params$group must be one of: ", toString(colourable), "; not '",
    group_col, "'"
  )
}

grp <- samples[[group_col]]
if (anyNA(grp)) {
  grp <- factor(
    ifelse(is.na(grp), "NA", as.character(grp)),
    levels = c(levels(grp), "NA")
  )
}
samples$.group <- grp
group_colours <- level_colours(grp)
has_groups <- group_col != ".all"

pca_cols <- if (length(plot_cols) > 0) plot_cols else ".all"
```

```{r QoL-functions}
# "a", "a and b", "a, b and c"
enum <- function(x) {
  if (length(x) <= 1) return(x)
  paste(paste(x[-length(x)], collapse = ", "), "and", x[length(x)])
}

# A data frame as a markdown table, for chunks with output: asis
cat_table <- function(d, ...) {
  cat(knitr::kable(d, row.names = FALSE, ...), sep = "\n")
  cat("\n")
}

# The variable with the largest R2 for one PC, as text
best_assoc <- function(pc) {
  a <- qc$pc_assoc[qc$pc_assoc$pc == pc & !is.na(qc$pc_assoc$r2), ]
  if (nrow(a) == 0) return("no variable")
  best <- a[which.max(a$r2), ]
  sprintf("%s (R^2^ = %.2f)", best$variable, best$r2)
}

var_pct <- qc$pca$var_pct
pc_names <- grep("^PC[0-9]+$", colnames(samples), value = TRUE)

# Label flagged samples, and every sample when there are few
samples$label <- ifelse(
  samples$flagged | n_samples <= params$max_labels,
  samples$sample,
  ""
)

theme_qc <- theme_linedraw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

# Markdown link to the NCBI gene page, searched by the Ensembl ID without
# its version; the ID is shown when there is no gene name
ncbi_link <- function(id, name) {
  id <- sub("^(ENS[A-Z]*G[0-9]+)\\.[0-9]+$", "\\1", id)
  name <- ifelse(is.na(name) | name == "", id, name)
  sprintf("[*%s*](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/?term=%s)", name, id)
}
```

`r n_samples` samples with both metadata and a quantification were checked, on `r comma(qc$genes[["with_reads"]])` genes with at least one read. **`r n_flagged` `r if (n_flagged == 1) "sample was" else "samples were"` flagged** for deviating from the rest (@tbl-summary). The checks do not use the experimental design, so a flag says that a sample differs from the others, not why.

```{r tbl-summary}
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste0("Per-sample metrics over the ", n_samples, " samples. Flagged counts the samples more than ", cfg$mad, " median absolute deviations from the median, on the side given in the Method.")

knitr::kable(
  qc$summary,
  col.names = c("Metric", "Min", "Median", "Max", "Flagged"),
  align = "lrrrr",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r flagged-samples}
#| output: asis

if (n_flagged == 0) {
  cat("::: {.callout-tip title=\"No sample was flagged\"}\n")
  cat("All samples are within the limits on every metric.\n:::\n")
} else {
  cat("::: {.callout-warning title=\"Flagged samples\"}\n\n")
  flagged <- samples[samples$flagged, c("sample", ".group", "flags")]
  if (!has_groups) flagged$.group <- NULL
  cat_table(
    flagged,
    col.names = c("Sample", if (has_groups) group_col, "Flagged for")
  )
  cat("\n:::\n")
}

missing <- c(
  if (length(qc$checks$meta_only) > 0) {
    paste0(
      "**In the metadata, without a quantification:** ",
      toString(qc$checks$meta_only)
    )
  },
  if (length(qc$checks$quant_only) > 0) {
    paste0(
      "**Quantified, but not in the metadata:** ",
      toString(qc$checks$quant_only)
    )
  }
)
if (length(missing) > 0) {
  cat("\n::: {.callout-warning title=\"Samples left out\"}\n\n")
  cat(missing, sep = "\n\n")
  cat("\n\n:::\n")
}
```

::: {.callout-note title="Method" collapse=true}

Gene-level counts were imported from the salmon quantifications with tximport (v`r cfg$versions[["tximport"]]`) and checked without the experimental design (DESeq2 v`r cfg$versions[["DESeq2"]]`, design `~ 1`).

- **Library size** is the number of reads assigned to genes, and **mapping rate** the share of the processed reads that salmon mapped.
- **Detected genes** have at least one read. The **top-10 share** is the share of a sample's reads in its 10 most abundant genes; a high share means a few genes dominate the library, which leaves fewer reads for the rest.
- **PCA** used the variance-stabilised counts (vst, blind to the design) of the `r comma(cfg$ntop)` most variable genes, as in `DESeq2::plotPCA()`. Each principal component was regressed on every metadata column and technical metric; R^2^ is the share of the component's variance that the variable explains.
- **Correlations** between samples are Spearman correlations of the variance-stabilised counts of the `r comma(qc$genes[["expressed"]])` genes with at least `r cfg$min_count` reads in half of the samples. Samples were clustered on 1 − correlation with average linkage. A sample's **median correlation** is the median over all other samples.
- **Metadata columns** were compared in pairs with Cramér's V, which is 0 when two columns are unrelated and 1 when one determines the other.
- **Flags.** A sample is flagged when a metric is more than `r cfg$mad` median absolute deviations from the median on the bad side: a low library size (log~10~), mapping rate, number of detected genes or median correlation, or a high top-10 share.

:::

# Samples and metadata

```{r tbl-groups}
#| tbl-cap: "Samples per level of each metadata column. Continuous columns show their range."

group_rows <- lapply(cfg$columns, function(col) {
  x <- samples[[col]]

  if (is.numeric(x)) {
    return(data.frame(
      Column = col,
      Level = sprintf(
        "%s – %s",
        format(min(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
        format(max(x, na.rm = TRUE))
      ),
      Samples = sum(!is.na(x))
    ))
  }

  n <- table(x, useNA = "ifany")
  lvl <- names(n)
  lvl[is.na(lvl)] <- "(missing)"
  data.frame(Column = col, Level = lvl, Samples = as.integer(n))
})

do.call(rbind, group_rows) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "llr", row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r confounding-setup}
conf <- qc$confounding
conf <- conf[order(conf$cramers_v, decreasing = TRUE), ]

# Pairs that a model cannot separate, or hardly
is_confounded <- conf$nested != "" | conf$cramers_v >= 0.8
conf_pairs <- paste(conf$column_1, conf$column_2, sep = " x ")[is_confounded]
```

When two metadata columns split the samples in the same way, their effects cannot be told apart: a difference between the groups of one column could equally come from the other. This matters most when a column of interest lines up with a batch, such as a collection date or a sequencing run. Of the `r nrow(conf)` pairs of categorical columns, `r sum(is_confounded)` `r if (sum(is_confounded) == 1) "is" else "are"` nested or strongly related (Cramér's V ≥ 0.8). Columns that are derived from each other, such as a group and the season it belongs to, are expected here.

```{r tbl-confounding}
#| eval: !expr nrow(conf) > 0
#| tbl-cap: "Pairs of categorical metadata columns, sorted by Cramér's V (0 = unrelated, 1 = one column determines the other). Nested shows when every level of one column occurs with a single level of the other."

knitr::kable(
  conf,
  col.names = c("Column 1", "Column 2", "Samples", "Cramér's V", "Nested"),
  align = "llrrl",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r confounding-crosstabs}
#| output: asis

if (length(conf_pairs) > 0) {
  cat("::: {.callout-note title=\"Cross-tables of the related columns\"")
  cat(" collapse=true}\n\n")
  for (pair in conf_pairs) {
    tab <- qc$crosstabs[[pair]]
    d <- as.data.frame.matrix(tab)
    d <- cbind(setNames(data.frame(rownames(d)), pair), d)
    cat_table(d)
  }
  cat("\n:::\n")
}
```

# Sequencing depth and complexity

```{r metric-data}
metric_lab <- c(
  library_size = "Library size (million reads)",
  pct_mapped = "Mapping rate (%)",
  detected_genes = "Detected genes",
  top10_pct = "Reads in the 10 most abundant genes (%)",
  median_cor = "Median correlation with the other samples"
)

m <- samples
m$library_size <- m$library_size / 1e6

# Metrics that were measured, e.g. no mapping rate without meta_info.json
metrics <- names(metric_lab)[vapply(names(metric_lab), function(k) {
  !all(is.na(m[[k]]))
}, logical(1))]

# The same horizontal offset for a sample in every panel
set.seed(1337)
offset <- runif(n_samples, -0.18, 0.18)

metric_long <- do.call(rbind, lapply(metrics, function(k) {
  data.frame(
    sample = m$sample,
    group = m$.group,
    x = as.numeric(m$.group) + offset,
    flagged = m$flagged,
    metric = metric_lab[[k]],
    value = m[[k]]
  )
}))
metric_long$metric <- factor(metric_long$metric, levels = metric_lab[metrics])

metric_fig_h <- 1 + 2.8 * ceiling(length(metrics) / 2)
```

@fig-metrics shows each metric per sample. Samples within a group should be at a similar level; a sample far below its group in library size, mapping rate or detected genes, or far above in the top-10 share, has a library of lower quality or complexity.

```{r fig-metrics}
#| fig-cap: !expr paste0("Per-sample metrics", if (has_groups) paste0(" by ", group_col) else "", ". Each point is a sample and the line the group median. Flagged samples are labelled.")
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: !expr metric_fig_h

p <- ggplot(metric_long, aes(x, value)) +
  stat_summary(
    aes(x = as.numeric(group), group = group),
    fun = median,
    fun.min = median,
    fun.max = median,
    geom = "crossbar",
    width = 0.55,
    linewidth = 0.3,
    colour = "grey30"
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(fill = group),
    shape = 21,
    size = 2.8,
    stroke = 1,
    colour = "grey20",
    alpha = 0.85
  ) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = metric_long[metric_long$flagged, ],
    aes(label = sample),
    size = 2.8,
    colour = "grey30",
    max.overlaps = Inf,
    seed = 1337
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ metric, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq_along(levels(m$.group)),
    labels = levels(m$.group)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = group_colours, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_qc +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1)
  )

print(p)
```

The number of detected genes normally rises with the library size along one curve (@fig-depth). A sample below the curve has fewer genes than its depth would give, which points to low complexity rather than low depth.

```{r fig-depth}
#| fig-cap: "Detected genes against library size. Labelled samples are flagged, or all samples when there are few."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 5

p <- ggplot(samples, aes(library_size / 1e6, detected_genes)) +
  geom_point(
    aes(fill = .group),
    shape = 21,
    size = 3.5,
    stroke = 0.4,
    colour = "grey20",
    alpha = 0.85
  ) +
  geom_text_repel(
    aes(label = label),
    size = 3,
    colour = "grey30",
    max.overlaps = Inf,
    seed = 1337
  ) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = comma) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = group_colours,
    name = NULL,
    guide = if (has_groups) "legend" else "none"
  ) +
  labs(x = "Library size (million reads, log scale)", y = "Detected genes") +
  theme_qc +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

print(p)
```

# Count distribution

Every sample should have a similar distribution of counts. A curve shifted to the left has more genes with few reads, and a different shape points to a different library composition (@fig-density).

```{r fig-density}
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of the gene counts per sample, as log2 counts per million (CPM + 1), for genes with at least one read in any sample. Flagged samples are drawn with a thicker line."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

dens <- qc$density
i <- match(dens$sample, samples$sample)
dens$group <- samples$.group[i]
dens$flagged <- samples$flagged[i]

p <- ggplot(dens, aes(x, y, group = sample, colour = group)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line(data = dens[dens$flagged, ], linewidth = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = group_colours,
    name = NULL,
    guide = if (has_groups) "legend" else "none"
  ) +
  labs(x = expression(log[2] ~ (CPM + 1)), y = "Density") +
  theme_qc +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

print(p)
```

# Principal component analysis

```{r pca-functions}
# One PCA panel, filled by a metadata column
pca_plot <- function(col, i, j) {
  x <- paste0("PC", i)
  y <- paste0("PC", j)
  is_num <- is.numeric(samples[[col]])
  legend_name <- if (col == ".all") NULL else col

  p <- if (is_num) {
    ggplot(samples, aes(.data[[x]], .data[[y]], fill = .data[[col]])) +
      geom_point(
        shape = 21,
        size = 4,
        stroke = 0.4,
        colour = "grey20",
        alpha = 0.85
      ) +
      scale_fill_gradient(
        low = seq_low,
        high = seq_high,
        na.value = na_colour,
        name = legend_name
      )
  } else {
    ggplot(
      samples,
      aes(.data[[x]], .data[[y]], fill = .data[[col]], shape = .data[[col]])
    ) +
      geom_point(size = 4, stroke = 0.4, colour = "grey20", alpha = 0.85) +
      scale_fill_manual(
        values = level_colours(samples[[col]]),
        na.value = na_colour,
        name = legend_name
      ) +
      scale_shape_manual(
        values = level_shapes(samples[[col]]),
        na.value = 21,
        name = legend_name
      )
  }

  p +
    geom_text_repel(
      aes(.data[[x]], .data[[y]], label = label),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      size = 3,
      colour = "grey30",
      max.overlaps = Inf,
      seed = 1337
    ) +
    labs(
      x = sprintf("%s (%.1f%%)", x, var_pct[i]),
      y = sprintf("%s (%.1f%%)", y, var_pct[j])
    ) +
    theme_qc
}

# PC1 vs PC2, and PC3 vs PC4 when there are that many components
pca_panels <- function(col) {
  p <- pca_plot(col, 1, 2)
  if (all(c("PC3", "PC4") %in% pc_names)) p <- p + pca_plot(col, 3, 4)

  p +
    plot_layout(guides = "collect") &
    theme(legend.position = if (col == ".all") "none" else "bottom")
}

scree <- data.frame(
  pc = factor(seq_along(var_pct), levels = seq_along(var_pct)),
  var_pct = var_pct
) |>
  head(10)
```

The first two principal components explain `r sprintf("%.1f", var_pct[1])` % and `r sprintf("%.1f", var_pct[2])` % of the variance of the `r comma(cfg$ntop)` most variable genes (@fig-scree). PC1 is most strongly associated with `r best_assoc("PC1")` and PC2 with `r best_assoc("PC2")`.

```{r fig-scree}
#| fig-cap: "Variance explained by the first principal components."
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 3.5

p <- ggplot(scree, aes(pc, var_pct)) +
  geom_col(fill = series_colours[1], width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%.1f", var_pct)),
    vjust = -0.4,
    size = 3.2,
    colour = "grey20"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  labs(x = "Principal component", y = "Variance explained (%)") +
  theme_qc +
  theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())

print(p)
```

The tabs below show the same PCA coloured by each metadata column. Samples should group by the variable of interest, and not by a technical one. A sample far from its own group is worth a look in the table at the end.

```{r pca-tabs}
#| output: asis
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5.5

cat("::: {.panel-tabset}\n\n")
for (col in pca_cols) {
  cat("\n## ", if (col == ".all") "All samples" else col, "\n\n")
  print(pca_panels(col))
  cat("\n\n")
}
cat(":::\n")
```

## What the components reflect

```{r assoc-data}
assoc <- qc$pc_assoc[!is.na(qc$pc_assoc$r2), ]

pc_index <- as.integer(sub("PC", "", assoc$pc))
assoc$pc_lab <- sprintf("%s\n%.1f%%", assoc$pc, var_pct[pc_index])
assoc$pc_lab <- factor(
  assoc$pc_lab,
  levels = unique(assoc$pc_lab[order(pc_index)])
)
assoc$variable <- factor(assoc$variable, levels = rev(unique(assoc$variable)))
assoc$type <- factor(assoc$type, levels = c("metadata", "technical"))

sig <- !is.na(assoc$padj) & assoc$padj < 0.05
assoc$label <- paste0(sprintf("%.2f", assoc$r2), ifelse(sig, "*", ""))

assoc_fig_h <- max(3, 1.6 + 0.4 * nlevels(assoc$variable))

# Technical metrics that explain much of PC1 or PC2
technical_pcs <- assoc[
  assoc$type == "technical" & assoc$pc %in% c("PC1", "PC2") &
    assoc$r2 >= 0.5 & sig,
]
```

@fig-assoc shows how much of each component every metadata column and technical metric explains. A component that follows the variable of interest is what the study hopes for. One that follows a technical metric, or a batch column, shows unwanted variation that the model of the differential expression analysis should account for.

```{r technical-warning}
#| output: asis

if (nrow(technical_pcs) > 0) {
  cat("::: {.callout-warning title=\"A main component follows a technical")
  cat(" metric\"}\n\n")
  cat(sprintf(
    "- %s: %s (R^2^ = %.2f)\n",
    technical_pcs$pc,
    technical_pcs$variable,
    technical_pcs$r2
  ), sep = "")
  cat(
    "\nCheck whether the metric differs between the groups (@fig-metrics):",
    "if it does, group differences and library quality are hard to tell",
    "apart.\n\n:::\n"
  )
}
```

```{r fig-assoc}
#| eval: !expr nrow(assoc) > 0
#| fig-cap: "Share of each principal component's variance explained by the metadata columns and the technical metrics (R^2^ of a linear model of the component on the variable). * adjusted p-value < 0.05 (F-test, Benjamini–Hochberg over all tests)."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: !expr assoc_fig_h

p <- ggplot(assoc, aes(pc_lab, variable, fill = r2)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_text(aes(label = label, colour = r2 > 0.55), size = 3.4) +
  facet_grid(type ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = seq_low,
    high = seq_high,
    limits = c(0, 1),
    name = expression(R^2)
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(`TRUE` = "white", `FALSE` = "grey15"),
    guide = "none"
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_qc +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

print(p)
```


# Sample clustering

Samples from the same group are expected to correlate best with each other and to cluster together (@fig-heatmap, @fig-dendrogram). The lowest correlation between two samples is `r sprintf("%.3f", min(qc$cor))`.

```{r heatmap-data}
clust_order <- qc$clustering$labels[qc$clustering$order]
show_names <- n_samples <= 50

cor_long <- data.frame(
  s1 = rep(rownames(qc$cor), times = ncol(qc$cor)),
  s2 = rep(colnames(qc$cor), each = nrow(qc$cor)),
  r = as.vector(qc$cor)
)
cor_long$s1 <- factor(cor_long$s1, levels = clust_order)
cor_long$s2 <- factor(cor_long$s2, levels = rev(clust_order))

# One annotation row above the heat map per metadata column, at most three
strip_cols <- head(colourable, 3)

strip_plot <- function(col) {
  d <- data.frame(
    sample = factor(samples$sample, levels = clust_order),
    value = samples[[col]]
  )

  ggplot(d, aes(sample, 1, fill = value)) +
    geom_raster() +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = level_colours(samples[[col]]),
      na.value = na_colour,
      name = col
    ) +
    scale_x_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = 1, labels = col, expand = c(0, 0)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks = element_blank(),
      panel.grid = element_blank()
    )
}
```

```{r fig-heatmap}
#| fig-cap: !expr paste0("Spearman correlation between the samples, ordered by hierarchical clustering (average linkage on 1 − correlation)", if (length(strip_cols) > 0) paste0(". The rows above the heat map show ", enum(strip_cols), " for each sample") else "", if (show_names) "." else ". Sample names are left out because there are more than 50 samples.")
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 8.5

heat <- ggplot(cor_long, aes(s1, s2, fill = r)) +
  geom_raster() +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = seq_low,
    high = seq_high,
    name = "Spearman\ncorrelation"
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )

if (!show_names) heat <- heat + theme(axis.text = element_blank())

p <- wrap_plots(
  c(lapply(strip_cols, strip_plot), list(heat)),
  ncol = 1,
  heights = c(rep(0.035, length(strip_cols)), 1)
) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect")

print(p)
```

```{r fig-dendrogram}
#| fig-cap: !expr paste0("Hierarchical clustering of the samples (average linkage on 1 − Spearman correlation)", if (has_groups) paste0(". Points show the ", group_col, " of each sample.") else ".")
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5.5

leaf_colour <- setNames(
  unname(group_colours[as.character(samples$.group)]),
  samples$sample
)

dend <- dendrapply(as.dendrogram(qc$clustering), function(node) {
  if (is.leaf(node)) {
    attr(node, "nodePar") <- list(
      pch = 19,
      cex = 0.9,
      col = leaf_colour[[attr(node, "label")]],
      lab.cex = 0.7
    )
  }
  node
})

par(mar = c(if (n_samples <= 60) 8 else 2, 4, 1, 1))
plot(
  dend,
  ylab = "1 − Spearman correlation",
  leaflab = if (n_samples <= 60) "perpendicular" else "none"
)
if (has_groups) {
  legend(
    "topright",
    legend = names(group_colours),
    col = group_colours,
    pch = 19,
    bty = "n",
    cex = 0.8
  )
}
```

# All samples

Every sample with its metadata and metrics; flagged samples are highlighted. Click on a column to sort by it.

```{r tbl-samples}
#| column: screen

metric_cols <- c(
  "library_size", "pct_mapped", "detected_genes", "top10_pct",
  "size_factor", "median_cor"
)
tbl <- samples[, c("sample", cfg$columns, metric_cols, "flags")]

reactable(
  tbl,
  columns = list(
    sample = colDef(name = "Sample", minWidth = 120),
    library_size = colDef(
      name = "Library size",
      format = colFormat(separators = TRUE)
    ),
    pct_mapped = colDef(name = "Mapped (%)"),
    detected_genes = colDef(
      name = "Detected genes",
      format = colFormat(separators = TRUE)
    ),
    top10_pct = colDef(name = "Top-10 share (%)"),
    size_factor = colDef(name = "Size factor"),
    median_cor = colDef(name = "Median cor."),
    flags = colDef(name = "Flagged for", minWidth = 160)
  ),
  rowStyle = function(index) {
    if (tbl$flags[index] != "") list(background = flag_colour)
  },
  filterable = TRUE,
  defaultPageSize = 15,
  striped = FALSE,
  highlight = TRUE,
  compact = TRUE,
  theme = reactableTheme(cellPadding = "4px 6px")
)
```
